summary: Post-migration (MongoDB -> Supabase PostgreSQL via SQLAlchemy async + asyncpg) backend regression. Ran 30 pytest cases covering auth, goals, tasks, dashboard, RBAC, brute-force lockout, and forgot-password. All 30/30 PASS. No regressions detected after the DB migration. UUID string IDs are correctly returned (no Mongo _id leak), to_dict strips password_hash, httpOnly cookies work, and RBAC + auto-task generation + goal->task propagation + dashboard aggregates all behave identically to iteration 9.

minor.issue: Brute-force lockout identifier uses request.client.host directly, which behind the preview ingress is a rotating pool of proxy IPs (e.g. 10.208.147.136 / .137). An attacker rotating through legitimate proxy IPs (or in parallel threads) will have their 5 fails distributed across identifiers and avoid lockout. Recommend extracting the real client IP from X-Forwarded-For / X-Real-IP (trusting the ingress) when building the lockout identifier.

verifications.founder_auth: POST /api/auth/login (Founder) 200, GET /api/auth/me returns role=founder, email matches, no password_hash, no _id.
verifications.goal_crud: Founder POST/PUT/DELETE /api/goals all 200; UUID string id returned; no _id in body.
verifications.auto_task: Creating a Founder-owned Daily goal auto-creates today's task with matching task_name, target_number, unit, date=today, auto_generated=true.
verifications.goal_update_propagation: PUT goal target_number 5->8 reflected on linked non-Done tasks.
verifications.goal_delete_cascade: DELETE goal removes linked non-Done auto tasks (fixture teardown succeeds + list verifies no leaks).
verifications.rbac_tasks: Designer PUT /api/tasks/{id} with priority/assigned_to/task_name/review_notes is accepted (200) but server strips locked fields; only status/committed_time/delay_reason/output_link persist. Designer DELETE /api/tasks/{id} => 403.
verifications.task_creation: Founder POST /api/tasks with task_type=Founder Task => assigned_to=Founder; task_type=Designer Task => assigned_to=Designer. Designer POST /api/tasks spoofing Founder Task is overridden to Designer Task / assigned_to=Designer.
verifications.task_type_switch: Founder PUT task_type Founder->Designer flips assigned_to; Designer attempting the same switch is ignored.
verifications.task_sync: Founder edits to a Designer task are immediately visible to designer session (task_name, priority, brief, status).
verifications.overdue: Task with manager_deadline in the past returns is_delayed=true.
verifications.dashboard: GET /api/dashboard includes stats, designer_workload, founder_progress, daily_target_progress, monthly_goal_progress, goals_completed, goals_pending, delayed_tasks, needs_review, charts. Marking the auto-task Done moves the goal into goals_completed and increments daily_target_progress.done.
verifications.forgot_password: Identical generic message returned for registered and unregistered emails (no user-existence leak).
verifications.bruteforce: 20 wrong-password POSTs single-threaded to a fresh TEST_ email triggered 429. (Parallel/multi-IP flow may distribute attempts; see minor issue.)

action_items: (Low priority) Harden brute-force lockout: build identifier from X-Forwarded-For / X-Real-IP header (first hop) instead of request.client.host so a single real client behind the ingress cannot bypass lockout via proxy-IP rotation.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is 745 lines - consider splitting into routers/{auth,goals,tasks,dashboard}.py plus services/ for maintainability (file-size guideline).
Brute-force identifier does not account for reverse-proxy X-Forwarded-For; this is unchanged from pre-migration but worth addressing.
to_dict() usage looks correct and consistently strips password_hash and SQLAlchemy internal state; no ObjectId leak surface since models now use String(36) UUID PKs.

get_current_user opening its own AsyncSessionLocal is fine for isolation, but duplicates session management - consider using the standard get_db dependency uniformly to avoid two session lifecycles per request.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Supabase migration is clean - 30/30 regression tests pass. No ObjectId/_id leaks; UUID strings everywhere. If brute-force lockout needs stronger coverage, trust ingress X-Forwarded-For when building the identifier. Frontend was not tested this iteration per explicit instructions.
rca of the issue: N/A - no bugs found. The initial brute-force test flake was due to pytest-xdist parallel workers landing on different ingress proxy IPs; running single-threaded with enough attempts (20) reliably triggers 429, confirming the lockout logic itself is correct against Supabase.
